conventions: יָחַשׂ (hithpael, 'enrol by genealogy') rendered with a supplied English noun that writes its lexeme — 'the genealogy be reckoned' (5.1), 'the genealogy was reckoned' (5.7), 'were reckoned by genealogies' (5.17) — is one unit on the verb under rule 44's lexeme-carrying-noun clause, headed on genealogy/genealogies, not a supplied subject noun marked added under rule 17. The competing reading (noun added, head on reckoned) is named in each note; a later chapter that meets this verb should read the corpus for it before departing.

The specifying לְ of וַיַּגְלֵם לָראוּבֵנִי וְלַגָּדִי וְלַחֲצִי (5.26) takes the ASV's appositional 'even' under rule 11, since it stands on the very phrase the word introduces; the repeated לְ on each later member, for which the ASV writes only the waw's 'and', is unrepresented under rule 40.

Two-token proper names (Baal | meon, Baal | hermon, Tilgath | pilneser) are split token to English word; where the name is a rectum the chain's 'of' joins the first token (5.26 'of Tilgath'), and where the ASV writes no 'of' both tokens are bare (5.6).
report: Read all 26 verses end to end against the 42-lemma candidate table. Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by the ASV's own wording (waw → and/but/even/with/who; suffix → their/them/these; כִּי → for/because; עַד → unto/until) or by a different construction in the source (5.8 וְעַד splits even|unto on waw|עַד while 5.9's waw-less עַד holds even unto whole, rule 16; 5.8 הוּא → who vs 5.10 waw → who, the two sides of rule 17).

The one construction that recurs across three verses — יָחַשׂ rendered 'the genealogy be/was reckoned' (5.1, 5.7) and 'were reckoned by genealogies' (5.17) — is treated the same way each time: the supplied noun carries the verb's lexeme and joins the verb's unit under rule 44, headed on genealogy/genealogies, with the 'the genealogy added, head reckoned' alternative named in every note. Recorded as a convention.

Chain-with-possessive family (fathers' houses, 5.13/15/24) is uniform: לְ → of, בֵית → houses (or of houses where it is the rectum of רָאשֵׁי), אָב → fathers. Half-tribe formula (5.18/23/26) uniform: שֵׁבֶט bare tribe under rule 28, name takes of. Two-token names split token-to-word in 5.6/8/23/26, the rectum's of joining the first token in 5.26.

BSB disagreements: all seven are documented convention differences — recast לְ left bare (5.2, 5.9 after עַד holds even unto, 5.26 repeated appositional לְ), articles on toponyms and on הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה, the thousand/hundred waw of 5.18 under rule 42, and a bare-object אֵת. None is an error.

No added units in the chapter; checked that none was avoided by folding: 5.20's 'put their trust' keeps the possessive inside the light-verb idiom with the rule-18 alternative noted, and 5.10's italic 'land' sits on פְּנֵי with the alternative noted. Both are single-verse judgments, not splits. No promotion: the chapter teaches nothing the corpus shown confirms as general.
